LESSON: PUNCTUATIO NS AND INDICATORS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Germa n Braille
Topic 9.3: Punctuatio ns and Indicators
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Punctuatio ns and Indicators, part of Germa n Braille in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use punctuation marks when writing braille work? 2. How do you differentiate punctuation marks from letters of the alphabet?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Punctuatio ns and Indicators together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Peace: This is achieved as learners work together in

harmony in their groups to read and write sentences with

punctuation marks.

Link to other Learning Areas:

German: This is achieved as learners use the acquired

skills to punctuate sentences in German.

Suggested Community Service Learning:

Learners could make cards bearing different punctuations in

print and braille, and then challenge their sighted playmates

to identify the number and position of dots of the

punctuation marks.

Learning: Learners could look for children’s

Suggested Assessment:

Peer assessment, oral assessment and written assessment.
